hypotheses.paper: x ∈ 2A_2+1, A_2 the 2-completion of a Z/2Z-ring, claimed ≅ Z_2 at l.52
hypotheses.note: a reading: stated over Z_2 = PadicInt 2 directly, as the dispatch fixes; the map A → Z_2 and A_2 ≅ Z_2 are T-syr-completion's

theo_rep is on RepDomain = {x odd | ∀ k, 3T^k(x)+1 ≠ 0}, i.e. 2Z_2+1 minus the backward T-orbit of -1/3; the printed form is false there (Finding 1). In Z every odd x is in RepDomain (Syracuse.three_mul_add_one_ne_zero)
RepSeq = {q | q 0 = 0 ∧ StrictMono q}; ↗↗ read as strictly increasing, as in T-syr-base
repInv q = -inv3 * ∑' n, 2^(q n) * inv3^n, inv3 the inverse of the unit 3 of Z_2; the series converges (terms of norm ≤ 2^{-n}, Syracuse.summable_rep)

findings: syracuse.tex:88–90 — false as printed on 2A_2+1 = 2Z_2+1: x0 = -1/3 is odd but not in the image of the printed inverse φ^{-1} (Syracuse.neg_inv3_not_mem_image), nor is any y_k = -(2^k+3)/9, k ≥ 1, which satisfies T(y_k) = -1/3 with ν_2(3y_k+1) = k (Syracuse.neg_third_preimage). Hence no map φ from 2Z_2+1 to {p | p_0 = 0, p ↗↗} has the printed φ^{-1} as a left inverse, whatever values are given to the undefined p_n on the backward orbit of -1/3 (Syracuse.rep_printed_false). Strongest true form proved (Syracuse.theo_rep): φ: x ↦ (p_n(x)) is a bijection from RepDomain (odd x whose T-orbit avoids -1/3) onto the strictly increasing sequences from 0, its inverse is the printed formula, and the image of the formula is exactly RepDomain (Syracuse.repInv_image). This is the theorem-level form of OQ-42 (d).

syracuse.tex:92–95 — the proof establishes only φ^{-1} ∘ φ = id (x = -(1/3)Σ 2^{p_k(x)}/3^k, i.e. injectivity of φ); that every strictly increasing p with p_0 = 0 is some φ(x) (surjectivity, and that the printed formula lands in the domain) is not argued. It is proved here: S(q) = Σ 2^{q_n}/3^n satisfies S(q) = 1 + (1/3)2^{q_1}S(q') with q'_n = q_{n+1} - q_1 (Syracuse.repSeries_eq), so 3φ^{-1}(q)+1 = 2^{q_1}φ^{-1}(q') with φ^{-1}(q') odd, whence T(φ^{-1}q) = φ^{-1}q' and a_0(φ^{-1}q) = q_1 (Syracuse.T_repInv) and p_n(φ^{-1}q) = q_n (Syracuse.rep_repInv). The proof's displayed identity (l.93) also writes x ∈ 2A+1 where 2A_2+1 is meant, and holds only on orbits avoiding -1/3.
questions: theo:rep is stated for A_2, the completion of an unnamed Z/2Z-ring A, and l.52 claims A_2 ≅ Z_2 (false for A = Z/2Z, T-syr-base). Reading taken (fixed by the dispatch): Z_2 itself. Whether theo:rep should be read in A_2 for each A, or in Z_2 once and for all, is for the author; the injectivity half is proved in every Z/2Z-ring A without completion (Syracuse.rep_injOn, Syracuse.eq_of_p_eq).

Which corrected domain does the author intend for φ: 2A_2+1 minus the backward T-orbit of -1/3 (the form proved), or a domain change in def:ring_define (OQ-42 (d))? The mark waits on that ruling; a corrected form is not marked.

questions: The statement is proved with no added hypothesis (all x ∈ A, all n, every Z/2Z-ring, no 2 ≠ 0), but about the total maps T, a of T-syr-base, whose values at -1/3 are junk (OQ-42 (d), open). When 2 ≠ 0 the junk is never reached on either side (cycle_avoids_neg_third), so the author may rule the row closed without a corrected statement.
'periodic of period n' (l.98–99) is not defined: n a period, n the least period, or eventually periodic. No reading chosen: all three are proved.

hypotheses.paper: A_u^n of def:define_n__n_ (product to n-1-k, OQ-43)
hypotheses.note: Syracuse.Aun as printed (Aun_sub_ne_zero); the reading 'product to n-2-k' is proved too (AunAlt_sub_ne_zero)

findings: syracuse.tex:108 — false as printed: '∀ i, j ∈ ⟦1, n⟧' includes i = j, where A_i^n(a(x)) - A_j^n(a(x)) = 0, on every cycle; e.g. the cycle (1) of Z, n = 1, i = j = 1 (Syracuse.cor_ring_periodic_minimal_period_printed_false). For i ≠ j it holds in every Z/2Z-ring, with no 2 ≠ 0 (Syracuse.Aun_sub_ne_zero), for the printed A_u^n and for the off-by-one reading of OQ-43 (Syracuse.AunAlt_sub_ne_zero). Proof (the paper prints none): with x_u = T^u(x), on any orbit A_u^n(a(x)) = 2^{p_n(x_u)}(3x_{u+n}+1) - 3^n(3x_u+1) (Syracuse.Aun_cast_eq, from lem:base at n+1), so on a cycle A_u^n = (2^{p_n} - 3^n)(3x_u+1) as printed and (2^{p_n} - 3^n)x_u with the product to n-2-k (Syracuse.Aun_cast_of_cycle); 2^{p_n} - 3^n is odd since p_n ≥ 1 on a cycle, and x_1, ..., x_n are distinct by minimality. The corrected form is not vacuous: the cycle (-5, -7) of Z has least period 2 (Syracuse.cycle_neg_five).
questions: Is 'i ≠ j' intended (l.108)? Reading taken: the corrected form with i ≠ j is proved, unmarked; the printed form is refuted.

OQ-43 (product of A_u^n to n-1-k as printed, or n-2-k): not resolved; the corollary is proved under both. On a cycle the printed A_u^n is (2^{p_n} - 3^n)(3x_u+1) (Syracuse.Aun_cast_of_cycle), which confirms the T-syr-base audit's computation behind OQ-43 (gcd at least 2|2^{p_n} - 3^n|).

kb_proposals: Injectivity of x ↦ (p_n(x)) needs no completion: lem:base twice gives 3^n(x-y) = 2^{p_n}(T^n x - T^n y) (Syracuse.three_pow_mul_sub_eq), 2^j | 3^m z → 2^j | z holds in every ℤ/2ℤ-ring (Syracuse.two_pow_dvd_of_dvd_three_pow_mul, split on 2 = 0, else Prime 2), and Krull (IsZ2Ring.not_pow_succ_v2_dvd) closes: Syracuse.eq_of_p_eq (T-syr-rep).

Series in ℤ_[2]: Summable.of_norm_bounded summable_geometric_two with PadicInt.norm_units (‖unit‖ = 1) and simpa using PadicInt.norm_p (p := 2) (‖2‖ = 2⁻¹); split the first term with Summable.tsum_eq_zero_add and pull a factor with Summable.tsum_mul_left. 1/3 is ↑(isUnit_three_padicInt.unit⁻¹), with IsUnit.mul_val_inv (T-syr-rep).
On a cycle the total T never meets the junk when 2 ≠ 0: T(-1/3) = 0, T 0 = 1, T 1 = 1 ≠ -1/3 (Syracuse.cycle_avoids_neg_third); compute T on ℤ with T_unique, e.g. T(-5) = -7 (T-syr-rep).

The scaffold root SyracuseScaffold.lean was not edited (not in the dispatch): per lean-causal kb 0025 the master imports SyracuseScaffold.Rep there. Name clash avoided: the concurrent IntegerBounds.lean defines Syracuse.T_one_int, so Rep.lean defines none (T 1 = 1 is a local have); no other name of Rep.lean occurs in IntegerBounds.lean or the strict library.
